<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אייר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918574_theRebbe_925" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_99_D7_99_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918574_theRebbe_925__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the difference between attachment (deveikus) and connection (kesher), using the analogy of a belt versus a soul, and applies it to the distinction between sacrifices and incense.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And this will be understood by prefacing the known [concept]</t>
    <t s="2">that connection is also higher than attachment.</t>
    <t s="3">For attachment is in externality,</t>
    <t s="4">like when a belt clings to a man's loins,</t>
    <t s="5">that the attachment of the belt to</t>
    <t s="6">(the loins of)</t>
    <t s="7">the man is only to his externality,</t>
    <t s="8">whereas connection is in internality,</t>
    <t s="9">like "and his soul is bound to his soul"</t>
    <t s="10">which reaches into his innerness.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is the difference between sacrifices and incense,</t>
    <t s="12">that the service of sacrifices is from the aspect that Israel are attached to the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="13">[as it is brought in the Midrash</t>
    <t s="14">and in the Zohar],</t>
    <t s="15">and therefore they would offer the sacrifices upon the external altar,</t>
    <t s="16">which in the soul of man corresponds to the externality of the heart.</t>
    <t s="17">And incense is a term for connection</t>
    <t s="18">[for every "knot" in Scripture is translated as "ketar"],</t>
    <t s="19">and therefore the incense is upon the inner altar,</t>
    <t s="20">which in the soul of man corresponds to the innerness of the heart.</t>
    <t s="21">And the difference between the service of the externality of the heart and the service of the innerness of the heart is,</t>
    <t s="22">that the service of the externality of the heart is through reason and intellect,</t>
    <t s="23">for in love that is through reason and intellect, change applies,</t>
    <t s="24">whereas the service of the innerness of the heart is above reason and intellect,</t>
    <t s="25">in which no change applies.</t>
    <t s="26">And this is that "sacrifices" is a term for drawing near,</t>
    <t s="27">and "incense" a term for connection,</t>
    <t s="28">for "drawing near" indicates that it is a [separate] entity,</t>
    <t s="29">except that it is close to Divinity,</t>
    <t s="30">but it is possible that it may distance itself, Heaven forbid,</t>
    <t s="31">whereas connection</t>
    <t s="32">(incense)</t>
    <t s="33">is a permanent bond,</t>
    <t s="34">for the true meaning of a permanent bond is that no change applies to it.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section distinguishes between attachment and connection in the service from below to above (sacrifices and incense) and in the drawing down from above to below (Torah and charity).</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, this distinction between attachment and connection is in the service from below to above.</t>
    <t s="2">For sacrifices and incense are both the pillar of service,</t>
    <t s="3">which is an elevation from below to above.</t>
    <t s="4">And the distinction between attachment and connection regarding the drawing down from above to below</t>
    <t s="5">(Torah and acts of kindness)</t>
    <t s="6">is as it is brought in the Zohar:</t>
    <t s="7">"How beloved are Israel before the Holy One, blessed be He... and He desires to attach Himself to them and to connect with them."</t>
    <t s="8">And the Mitteler Rebbe explains</t>
    <t s="9">that "to attach Himself to them" is through the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="10">for the drawing down through the mitzvos is in the aspect of encompassing [light],</t>
    <t s="11">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="12">"and His right hand embraces me,"</t>
    <t s="13">that the light drawn down through the mitzvos embraces the person who performs the mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="14">for an embrace is from the outside,</t>
    <t s="15">and therefore it says "to attach Himself to them,"</t>
    <t s="16">for attachment is an external connection.</t>
    <t s="17">And "to connect with them" is through the Torah,</t>
    <t s="18">for the drawing down through the Torah is in internality, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="19">"and Your Torah is within my innards."</t>
    <t s="20">And therefore it says "and to connect with them,"</t>
    <t s="21">for connection is an internal connection.</t>
    <t s="22">For the connection of the Holy One, blessed be He, with Israel through the Torah is called "connection,"</t>
    <t s="23">as per the statement,</t>
    <t s="24">"Three knots</t>
    <t s="25">are connected one with another:</t>
    <t s="26">the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="27">the Torah, and Israel."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains two aspects of Israel's attachment to God—one regarding vessels (external unity) and one regarding lights (essential unity)—and why even the attachment of lights is called "attachment."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, regarding the attachment of Israel to the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="2">[from which aspect they have the power to offer sacrifices]</t>
    <t s="3">there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="4">For in the Midrash</t>
    <t s="5">it is brought that this that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded Israel to offer sacrifices is because they are attached to Me, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="6">"for as a belt clings to a man's loins," etc.</t>
    <t s="7">And in the Zohar</t>
    <t s="8">it is brought: "Fortunate are Israel, for the Holy One, blessed be He, called them 'Adam'... 'Adam, when one of you brings an offering,'</t>
    <t s="9">why did He call them 'Adam'? Because it is written,</t>
    <t s="10">'And you who cling to the Lord your God.'"</t>
    <t s="11">And it is explained in the continuation of 5666,</t>
    <t s="12">that the Midrash speaks about the matter of the attachment of vessels,</t>
    <t s="13">that the vessels are</t>
    <t s="14">in the aspect of [separate] existence, and their unity</t>
    <t s="15">(the attachment)</t>
    <t s="16">is not an essential unity,</t>
    <t s="17">and therefore it brings the verse "as a belt clings," etc., that the belt is an entity unto itself except that it is attached to the man,</t>
    <t s="18">whereas the Zohar speaks about the matter of the attachment of lights,</t>
    <t s="19">that the attachment and unity of lights is an essential unity,</t>
    <t s="20">and therefore it brings the verse "and you who cling to the Lord your God,"</t>
    <t s="21">a literal attachment.</t>
    <t s="22">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="23">that this that even the attachment of lights is called by the name "attachment,"</t>
    <t s="24">for attachment is in externality</t>
    <t s="25">(as above),</t>
    <t s="26">is because even the light is an extension and revelation that is outside the essence.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
